subject: Innova Health RFP: IP ownership, indemnity, and liability cap negotiation
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@innovahealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: James O'Connor <j.oconnor@innovahealth.com>, procurement@innovahealth.com
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Innova RFP - IP & liability questions (attached)

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we work through the RFP, our legal and procurement teams have a short set of follow-up questions focused on IP ownership, indemnity for third-party claims, and liability caps. I've attached the IP section of our RFP and highlighted the items that need vendor responses. High-level asks:

- Confirm whether Redwood claims any ownership of customer prompts/data or derivative outputs.
- Indemnity: we expect vendor indemnity for third-party IP infringement arising from the service.
- Liability cap: we typically propose a cap at 12 months of paid fees or $1M, whichever is greater.
- Order form: need clarity on termination for convenience, data return/destruction obligations, and any pass-through subcontractors.

Can you provide a redline of the proposed order form and a short memo on IP/indemnity positions by EOD Friday? Happy to set up a call if helpful.

Best,
Sarah
Senior Counsel, Innova Health

Attachment: Innova_RFP_IP_Questions.pdf

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Innova RFP - IP & liability questions (please advise)

Team - forwarding Innova's note. They want a redline + memo by EOD Friday. High priority: IP ownership language and the liability cap ask (12 months fees / $1M). Laura / Karthik, can legal ops confirm acceptable indemnity carve-outs? Marissa, want to ensure pricing/commitment implications if we need to accept a higher cap.

Proposed plan:
- Laura: draft a short memo with our positions on IP and indemnity (including usual carve-outs for open-source models and third-party content).
- Marissa: run the numbers for what a $1M cap or 12-month cap would cost on typical enterprise commit profiles.
- Karthik: prepare a redline of the Order_Form_Draft with our suggested language around termination, data handling, and subcontractor disclosures.

I'll coordinate responses to Sarah and offer a technical exceptions call if they want to dig into model behavior.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Innova RFP - IP & liability questions (please advise)

Rishi / team,

Draft memo below for quick internal review. I kept it short to hit Friday deadline. If we accept any Indy-style indemnity, we should ensure narrow scope and monetary caps. Key points:

1) IP ownership: Redwood does not claim ownership of customer prompts, data, or outputs. Customer retains ownership of their data and outputs. Redwood retains model weights, training artifacts, and platform code.

2) Indemnity for third-party IP claims: We can offer indemnity limited to infringement claims that result from our delivery of the service, subject to: (a) prompt notification by customer; (b) sole control of defense by Redwood; (c) customer cooperation; (d) exclusions for (i) customer modifications, (ii) customer-provided prompts that incorporate third-party content, and (iii) use cases involving models trained on public internet content where claims may arise.

3) Liability cap: Our standard cap is the greater of (i) 12 months of fees paid under the applicable Order Form, or (ii) $500,000. For strategic enterprise customers we can discuss a higher cap up to $1M, with pricing adjust. Any increase should be reflected in the committed spend or a one-time fee to broaden exposure.

4) Order form items: termination for convenience at renewal with 30 days' notice; for initial term, limited termination for convenience after 12 months; data return/destruction obligations within 60 days of termination; pass-through subcontractors must be listed in an annex and meet our SOC2/ISO controls.

I'm attaching a marked-up redline for the Order_Form_Draft (see Redwood_Response_Redline_v3.docx).

If everyone is ok, I can send to Sarah with the redline and a 1-page memo summarizing tradeoffs and pricing impact.

-L,
Laura
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Response_Redline_v3.docx

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@innovahealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: James O'Connor <j.oconnor@innovahealth.com>, procurement@innovahealth.com
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Innova RFP - IP & liability questions (attached)

Thanks Laura — that helps. A couple follow-ups from legal:

- Can you clarify the carve-out language for customer-provided prompts? Our concern is that customers who input third-party copyrighted content should not be able to shift infringement risk to vendors. We typically ask for an explicit statement that vendor indemnity does not cover customer-supplied content.
- On the liability cap: Innova has a strict policy for core patient-facing systems that sets a minimum $1M cap or 12 months fees, whichever is greater. Given this is a pilot for clinical triage, our GC needs the $1M floor.
- Order form: can Redwood accept 60-day data return + secure deletion and provide a deletion certificate? Also want an explicit subcontractor list or a certification that subcontractors meet the same security controls.

If you can accept these points, we can proceed to commercial redlines and DocuSign. If not, we should schedule a 30-minute call Friday to escalate.

Best,
Sarah

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 May 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Innova RFP - IP & liability questions (pricing impact)

Quick pricing note for internal thread:

- If we agree to a $1M floor (or greater of 12 months fees, $1M), modeled impact across a typical three-year enterprise subscription (monthly committed spend $40k) increases expected exposure ~2.5x versus our standard cap.
- Options to compensate: (1) increase monthly commitment (reserve additional dedicated capacity), (2) one-time fee to underwrite increased liability, or (3) narrower SOW scoping to exclude high-risk workloads (patient-identifiable triage models).

Recommendation: offer $1M cap but require either a 12-month committed minimum and a one-time liability underwrite fee equal to 0.5% of annual committed spend. That lets us accept the customer's ask while protecting unit economics.

-Marissa
Head of Revenue Operations

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@innovahealth.com>, James O'Connor <j.oconnor@innovahealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Innova RFP - Redwood responses and suggested commercial tradeoffs

Sarah / James — thanks for the patience. Attached are: (1) a 1-page memo summarizing our positions on IP, indemnity, and liability cap; (2) a marked Redline of your Order_Form_Draft; and (3) a pricing note on the commercial tradeoffs. Highlights below: 

- IP: Redwood confirms no claim to customer prompts/data/outputs. We retain model weights and platform code.
- Indemnity: Redwood will provide indemnity for third-party IP claims arising from our delivery of the Service, subject to the exclusions Laura noted (customer modifications, customer-supplied prompts containing third-party content, and public-data training exposures). We will drive the defense but will cooperate with Innova.
- Liability cap: We can accept your $1M floor (or greater of 12 months fees / $1M) for this pilot provided we implement one of the following commercial protections: (a) 12-month committed minimum; (b) one-time liability underwrite fee equal to 0.5% of the first year committed spend; or (c) restrict the initial pilot scope to non-patient-identifiable workloads.
- Data return/deletion: Redwood will return customer data within 60 days and provide deletion certification. Subcontractors: we will provide a subcontractor annex and confirm SOC2/ISO certifications for each listed provider.

If this is acceptable, I'll ask procurement to circulate a DocuSign-friendly redline and we can target signature by end of next week. If you'd like to chat, I'm happy to schedule a 30-minute call.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Response_Redline_v3.docx; Order_Form_Draft.pdf; Innova_RFP_IP_Questions.pdf
